paragraphs.en: The rough guide to marketing success used to be that you got what you paid for. No longer. While traditional “paid” media – such as television commercials and print advertisements – still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media. Consumers passionate about a product may create “earned” media by willingly promoting it to friends, and a company may leverage “owned” media by sending e-mail alerts about products and sales to customers registered with its Web site. The way consumers now approach the process of making purchase decisions means that marketing’s impact stems from a broad range of factors beyond conventional paid media.
paragraphs.zh: 过去，营销取得成功的一条粗略原则是：投入多少，就有多少回报。如今已不再如此。虽然电视广告和平面广告等传统“付费”媒体仍然发挥着重要作用，但今天的企业可以利用许多其他形式的媒体。对某种产品满怀热情的消费者，可能主动向朋友推荐它，从而创造“赢得的”媒体；企业也可以利用“自有”媒体，向在其网站注册的客户发送有关产品和促销活动的电子邮件通知。如今消费者作出购买决定的方式意味着，营销效果取决于传统付费媒体之外的诸多因素。

paragraphs.en: Paid and owned media are controlled by marketers promoting their own products. For earned media, such marketers act as the initiator for users’ responses. But in some cases, one marketer’s owned media become another marketer’s paid media – for instance, when an e-commerce retailer sells ad space on its Web site. We define such sold media as owned media whose traffic is so strong that other organizations place their content or e-commerce engines within that environment. This trend, which we believe is still in its infancy, effectively began with retailers and travel providers such as airlines and hotels and will no doubt go further. Johnson & Johnson, for example, has created BabyCenter, a stand-alone media property that promotes complementary and even competitive products. Besides generating income, the presence of other marketers makes the site seem objective, gives companies opportunities to learn valuable information about the appeal of other companies’ marketing, and may help expand user traffic for all companies concerned.
paragraphs.zh: 付费媒体和自有媒体由推广自身产品的营销者掌控。对于赢得的媒体，这类营销者则扮演引发用户反应的发起者角色。但在某些情况下，一个营销者的自有媒体会成为另一个营销者的付费媒体，例如电商零售商出售其网站上的广告位时。我们把这种“出售的媒体”定义为：流量大到足以吸引其他机构在其中投放内容或嵌入电子商务引擎的自有媒体。我们认为，这一趋势仍处于起步阶段；它实际上始于零售商以及航空公司、酒店等旅游服务提供者，而且无疑还会进一步发展。例如，强生公司创建了独立运营的媒体平台BabyCenter，推广与自身产品互补、甚至存在竞争关系的产品。其他营销者的入驻，除了带来收入，还使网站显得客观，为企业了解其他公司营销活动的吸引力提供有价值的信息，并可能帮助所有相关公司增加用户流量。

paragraphs.en: The same dramatic technological changes that have provided marketers with more (and more diverse) communications choices have also increased the risk that passionate consumers will voice their opinions in quicker, more visible, and much more damaging ways. Such hijacked media are the opposite of earned media: an asset or campaign becomes hostage to consumers, other stakeholders, or activists who make negative allegations about a brand or product. Members of social networks, for instance, are learning that they can hijack media to apply pressure on the businesses that originally created them.
paragraphs.zh: 剧烈的技术变革为营销者提供了更多、也更为多样的传播选择，同时也增加了一种风险：情绪强烈的消费者会以更迅速、更显眼、破坏性更大的方式表达意见。这种“被劫持的媒体”与赢得的媒体正好相反：一项媒体资产或营销活动，被那些对品牌或产品提出负面指控的消费者、其他利益相关者或活动人士所控制。例如，社交网络成员正在认识到，他们可以劫持媒体，向最初创建这些媒体的企业施压。

paragraphs.en: If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products, putting the reputation of the target company at risk. In such a case, the company’s response may not be sufficiently quick or thoughtful, and the learning curve has been steep. Toyota Motor, for example, alleviated some of the damage from its recall crisis earlier this year with a relatively quick and well-orchestrated social-media response campaign, which included efforts to engage with consumers directly on sites such as Twitter and the social-news site Digg.
paragraphs.zh: 如果出现这种情况，情绪强烈的消费者就会试图说服其他人抵制产品，使目标企业的声誉面临风险。在这种情况下，公司的反应可能不够迅速或周全，而掌握应对方法又相当困难。例如，丰田汽车通过一场比较迅速、组织有序的社交媒体应对活动，减轻了今年早些时候召回危机造成的部分损害；其措施包括在Twitter和社交新闻网站Digg等平台上，努力与消费者直接沟通。
